_comment: Hand-curated. Benchmark leaderboards publish long marketing names; the CLIs take short ids. The weekly benchmark pipeline lists every unmapped leaderboard model in its PR description instead of guessing a mapping, so a wrong alias never enters the routing table silently. One rule beyond that: an alias may only name the generation the CLI id resolves to today. `opus`, `sonnet` and `haiku` float to the current model, so a previous-generation benchmark row (claude-opus-4-6, grok-4) must not be aliased onto them - it would average a retired model into the score of the one the router actually spawns. Stale generations belong on the PR checklist, not in here.
